hypotheses.statement: solang rejects contracts using tx.origin at compile time with 'builtin tx.origin does not exist', while solc accepts them; pallet-contracts has no transaction-origin concept distinct from the caller.

evidence.note: solang compile failed: "builtin 'tx.origin' does not exist"; solc accepted the same source

hypotheses.next_probe: Compile a minimal contract whose only function returns tx.origin (address) and check solang_ok=false with the tx.origin error while solc_ok=true.

hypotheses.statement: solang rejects the blockhash(n) builtin at compile time ('unknown function or type blockhash'), whereas solc compiles it; pallet-contracts provides no EVM-style historical block hash.

evidence.note: solang compile failed: "unknown function or type 'blockhash'"; solc accepted

Minimal blockhash-only contract reproduced the prediction exactly: solang_ok=false with 'unknown function or type 'blockhash'' at the call site, solc_ok=true on identical source. Compile-time asymmetry, not a runtime value difference.

hypotheses.next_probe: Compile a minimal contract with a single function returning blockhash(block.number - 1) and verify solang rejects with the unknown-function error while solc accepts.

hypotheses.statement: block.number, block.timestamp, gasleft(), and msg.sender are all compilable under solang for pallet-contracts (they were not among the compile errors), but their runtime values may differ from solc/anvil semantics.

evidence.note: compile errors listed only tx.origin and blockhash; no error for block.number, block.timestamp, gasleft(), or msg.sender, implying those parse/resolve under solang

hypotheses.next_probe: Compile and run a stripped contract touching only block.number, block.timestamp, gasleft(), and msg.sender on both toolchains, storing the values and comparing them (excluding gas from the oracle); check whether both execute and whether block.number/timestamp values agree.
